summary: Frontend-only regression verification of the audio-race-condition fix in app/(tabs)/index.tsx (speak(), stopCloudTTS(), startRecording()). Tested via mobile web preview (375x667) since the actual Android APK OEM race condition cannot be reproduced in web preview. All requested flows pass: chat send + SSE streaming with citations works unchanged; speaker icon toggles correctly (volume-high-outline <-> stop-circle) on tap and re-tap with no crash; mic press-in correctly triggers the new defensive stopCloudTTS() call (speaker icon reverted to idle instantly when mic was pressed mid-playback); tab navigation (Ask/Rights/History/Settings) works with no regressions. No React Native red-screen errors or JS exceptions observed in console during any of the above.

integration_issues.flow: Hold-to-talk mic -> Whisper transcription (web preview only)
integration_issues.issue: After releasing the mic button, backend returns HTTP 422 on /api/voice/transcribe and no transcript modal or error Alert appears. Root cause is very likely that Playwright/headless Chromium's synthetic microphone stream produces an empty/invalid audio blob (not a code regression from this session's fix) -- this is a known web-preview limitation, not present in native builds. Flagging for awareness only; not caused by the speak()/stopCloudTTS()/startRecording() changes under review.

react_native_issues.issue: Console logs 'expo-file-system is not supported on web' twice per TTS attempt. Expected on web (File/Paths API is native-only) -- confirms the whole Cloud TTS playback path is a no-op on web preview by design, so the actual race-condition fix (createAudioPlayer -> isLoaded gating) can only be validated on a real native Android build, matching the review request's caveat. No crash resulted.

action_items: This fix (speak() isLoaded-gated play() + startRecording() defensive stopCloudTTS()) did NOT break any existing web-preview UI flow: chat streaming, citations, speaker toggle, mic press, and tab navigation all work correctly.

The actual bug being fixed (Android APK intermittent silent TTS playback) cannot be confirmed fixed without a new native Android build/APK test on a real device -- web preview cannot exercise expo-audio's native decode path.
No code changes were needed or made this session.
critical_code_review_comments: index.tsx is 1491 lines -- exceeds the 700-line guideline; consider extracting the TTS/STT logic (speak, stopCloudTTS, startRecording, stopRecording, and related refs) into a custom hook (e.g. useVoicePlayback / useVoiceRecording) for maintainability. Not a blocker for this fix, just a longer-term refactor suggestion.

speak()'s 2.5s hard-fallback timer and the isLoaded synchronous check are both reasonable defensive patterns for the described expo-audio race condition (github.com/expo/expo/discussions/18869); logic reads correctly and guards against superseded players via `ttsPlayerRef.current !== player` checks.

startRecording()'s new `stopCloudTTS()` call at the very top is correctly placed before any permission/await calls, so it always executes synchronously before the first await -- good placement for the defensive fix.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of requested flows pass in web preview (chat streaming, speaker toggle, mic defensive TTS-stop, tab navigation); APK-specific race condition unverifiable in this environment
